- Read prior progress at startup and saw this exact improve-code-boundaries task for tests/ha/support was already completed earlier as commit 8a5f85d with task switch already run.
- Loaded the improve-code-boundaries skill instructions and checked the current worktree state; current dirt is unrelated Ralph/skill files, not obvious pending edits in tests/ha/support.
- Verifying current HEAD and the tests/ha/support module contents before deciding whether anything new still needs to be changed.

- Verified HEAD is still 8a5f85d and the prior boundary collapse really removed tests/ha/support/runner, inlining the runtime/bootstrap entrypoint into tests/ha/support/mod.rs.
- Rather than assume the whole directory is done, started a fresh scan of tests/ha/support for the next single concrete boundary smell the skill would justify collapsing.
- Reading the support modules and grepping for wrapper/request/bootstrap/config/string-heavy patterns now.

- Explorer review found the next concrete boundary smell in tests/ha/support/world/mod.rs: the write-convergence attachment helper returns a nested tuple/result and the caller immediately reassembles WriteConvergenceState from it.
- Pivoting from the timeout-config candidate to this narrower smell-1 courier boundary because it is more local to tests/ha/support and removes a useless transition layer without inventing new abstractions.
- Reading the exact call/return path around wait_for_write_convergence_attachment and WriteConvergenceState before patching.

- Patched tests/ha/support/world/mod.rs to collapse the write-convergence attachment courier boundary: the helper now consumes WriteConvergenceStartup and returns a settled WriteConvergenceState instead of a nested tuple/result that the caller rebuilt by hand.
- The caller now only records the startup phase detail and stores the settled state, which removes one fake transition layer while preserving the same running/failed outcomes.
- Formatting next, then focused cargo nextest coverage for the touched path and make check for lint/compile verification.

- Verification caught a real lint issue from the refactor: pending_startup in tests/ha/support/world/mod.rs no longer needs mut, and clippy/nextest stop on -D warnings.
- No behavioral failures surfaced before compile stopped; fixing the unused mut and rerunning the same focused nextest and make check now.
- This is exactly why the repo instructions say not to ignore linters.

- Verification passed after the lint fix: focused cargo nextest ran the two affected write-convergence tests and both passed; make check also passed.
- Preparing to commit only tests/ha/support/world/mod.rs because the worktree contains many unrelated pre-existing Ralph/skill changes that must not be swept into this refactor.
- After the commit, I still need to run bash .ralph/task_switch.sh as requested and then report the resulting state.
